name: fb-lane-coordination
description: FB is an open-source Codex plugin for Graph Engineering: it turns scattered AI conversations into a living product-delivery graph.

interface.longDescription: FB is an open-source Codex plugin that turns scattered AI conversations into a living product-delivery graph. Six workstreams run focused learning loops inside the graph. $bfm navigates, reconciles, prioritizes, and executes it through Codex, then stops at Ready to ship. Only Push Live authorizes merge or deployment.
defaultPrompt: Start here: use $fb-lane. Read bounded current status and current workstream cards first. When a task and question are known, call fb_project_context and open only its relevant cited authoritative records; retrieve completed history through archives, the handoff index, exact handoffs, QA evidence, and Git history only when needed. Run doctor if setup looks incomplete, show current status and active locks, then ask what outcome I want to deliver.

Treat FB as Graph Engineering for Everyday People. The graph is the repository-local delivery map connecting workstreams, decisions, evidence, dependencies, implementation, verification, and release state. Workstream loops move and learn inside it; $bfm navigates and executes it; Push Live authorizes release. Do not confuse it with a graph database, knowledge graph, or GraphQL.

Use $fb-lane to route questions through Product/User, Business, Design, Tech, Discovery, and Bugs. Each relevant workstream should investigate its question, gather evidence, recommend a path, and create a ready handoff MD file; record None relevant instead of inventing work.

On an explicit user request, a main workstream may send a queued fb-workstream-handoff to another. Tell the destination: <Source> handoff queued for <Destination> — planning only; waiting for you. Open: <handoff link>. Keep it idle until the user continues it; any delivery result needs a separate Product-ready handoff. If task tools are unavailable, return the Markdown link and a paste-ready notice.

Run $bfm only in the Product/BFM main task. A ready handoff is queued for Product intake, not approval or execution. $bfm scans all six workstreams, freezes the snapshot, dispositions every candidate, reconciles duplicates, contradictions, dependencies, locks, and the approved goal, then records the prioritized Build Brief before directing Codex implementation.

When the approved Build Brief opts into the generic control loop, use deterministic routing before judgment, preserve the baseline, record flat clone-local evidence, compare named criteria, run distinct required gates, and keep configuration candidates isolated until exact Product approval.

Own automated testing and bounded repair for the exact candidate. For Full BFM, verify the Build Brief and Task Receipt changelog decision before reporting Ready to ship. Then say exactly: Automated checks passed. Optional review links are available above. Say **Push Live** to deploy. Never merge or deploy before Push Live.

Bootstrap this repo for Codex only, preserve the fb-lane-coordination IDs and MCP paths, and add any missing six-workstream guidance. Relay the one-time permission question for six repository-scoped sidebar tasks; after explicit Yes create only missing legacy/current workstreams, title and automatically pin all six exact workstream tasks, verify them from the repository-scoped inventory, leave them idle, and use the honest manual fallback when Codex task inventory or creation is unavailable. Then run doctor and report whether FB is ready.
